Q: Pandas Python - value_counts() or idxmax() returns different value each time A:

It seems there has been previous issues regarding how pandas value_counts() deals with tied values, in an inconsistent way.

As for idxmax() the documentation states clearly:

If multiple values equal the maximum, the first row label with that value is returned.

I am afraid the amount of information you provide is not enough for me to generate a full example with your data but here is an attempt:

import pandas as pd
data = {'col_1':['a','a','b','b','c','c'],'col_2':['one','two','three','one','two','three']}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)
for i in range(3):
    print(df['col_1'].value_counts().idxmax())

Run once in command:

c
c
c

Second time in command:

b
b
b

Third time:

a
a
a

The conclusion is that you are getting different values each time due to value_counts() and not idxmax(). Some solutions to make it always replicable is to use sort_index() too so that the output is not dependent on a random value. For example:

for i in range(3):
    print(df['col_1'].value_counts().sort_index().idxmax())

Returns always:

a
a
a

Q: IServiceScopeFactory vs IServiceProvider injecting into a singleton to call the CreateScope method A:

What's the actual problem you want answered? @null already answered, if you want to always use a scope, inject IServiceScopeFactory. IServiceProvider's CreateScope uses IServiceScopeFactory so there's no way that one would succeed while the other would fail.

The problems you may encounter are those you'd get if you request a scoped service in a singleton or long-lived service without a scope. But that's not what you asked.

Those problems are documented in the "Background Services" docs - you can end up with connection leaks, or trying to use an already disposed object (eg in web apps, where the request is a scope). You can also get errors in ASP.NET Core middleware as this blog post explains because middleware is created once and verifies the injected services. You can fix that without creating a scope if you inject in the method instead of the constructor

Q: Android build with newer AGP requiring gradle 9.2.0+ fails with early Settings_gradle error A:

Edric supplied the solution in a comment.

Gradle 9.2 and 9.3 are broken wrt. handling linked .gradle folder for cache on windows. It works in gradle 9.4+ when still using .gradle linked folder.

This is the related issue:
https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/35572

Thank you for updating the question! Unfortunately, my point still stands: we can't tell by looking at a random table whether that table design is scalable. It all depends on the queries you need to execute. Queries are determined by your business rquirements.
